nodes.label: FSL-1.1-MIT License
nodes.rationale: Functional Source License blocks competing commercial use while irrevocably granting an MIT license two years after each release, balancing commercial protection with eventual open licensing.

nodes.label: Auto Mode
nodes.rationale: Three autonomy tiers (Interactive/AutoPlan/FullAuto) cycled via Shift+Tab. The [security] config policy is a separate earlier check never bypassed by Auto Mode — the hard floor — and every auto-approved action is logged identically to manual approvals for a full audit trail.

nodes.label: Local LLM Support
nodes.rationale: 100% private (code never leaves the machine), zero API cost, and offline operation — also recommended as the compliant alternative to ToS-violating Claude Max / Copilot OAuth workarounds.

nodes.label: Ollama
nodes.rationale: Recommended local backend over LM Studio because it runs as an always-on daemon (no GUI to accidentally close), fitting Crustly's 10-second connect timeout and 90-second connection pool.

nodes.label: Native Ollama Provider
nodes.rationale: Speaks Ollama's native /api/chat protocol alongside the OpenAI-compatible route, unlocking runtime performance metrics, keep_alive/num_ctx control, and in-TUI model download/switch that the OpenAI shim cannot provide.

nodes.label: Phase 4 Tools (Claw Code Parity)
nodes.rationale: web_fetch, todo_write, ask_user, skill, agent, powershell bring full tool-set parity with Claw Code; sub-agents are recursion-safe — agents spawned by AgentTool cannot themselves spawn further sub-agents.

nodes.label: OS Keyring API Key Storage
nodes.rationale: API keys encrypted by the OS credential manager (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service) instead of plaintext files; keyring tried first with environment variables as fallback.

nodes.label: /skills and /mcp Discovery Commands
nodes.rationale: Intercepted before being sent to the LLM; a message starting with / that isn't a known command still goes to the LLM so file paths are not swallowed.

nodes.label: Kitty Keyboard Protocol Handling
nodes.rationale: Legacy terminals emit the same raw byte (0x0D) for Enter, Ctrl+Enter and Shift+Enter, so Shift+Enter newline requires Kitty protocol detection with an Alt+Enter fallback; the same ambiguity means Ctrl+M and Ctrl+I bindings are non-functional in legacy terminals — which is why Ctrl+O was chosen for Model Info instead of Ctrl+M.

nodes.label: Slash-Command Interception Layer
nodes.rationale: App::try_handle_slash_command runs on submit before send_message; unrecognized /... input falls through to the LLM as a normal message so legitimate slash-prefixed content (e.g. paths) is never swallowed; also fixed the bug where [[mcp.servers]] config was parsed but never connected.

nodes.label: tui-textarea Input Migration
nodes.rationale: Replaced the append-only String input buffer; uses input_without_shortcuts() because TextArea's built-in Emacs keymap Ctrl+letter bindings collide with crustly's global shortcuts; ratatui pinned to 0.26.3 in the committed lockfile to avoid two incompatible copies of the Widget trait.

nodes.label: Clipboard Copy/Paste Integration (arboard)
nodes.rationale: Ctrl+Y is one smart keybinding: copies the last fenced code block's raw content if present (via pulldown_cmark, not hand-rolled fence matching), otherwise the full response; Ctrl+V is the explicit paste fallback; both fail gracefully into error_message — arboard fails in ~3ms headless so no timeout wrapper needed.

nodes.label: Model Info Panel (Ctrl+O)
nodes.rationale: Shows provider, model, context window, and last-response PerfMetrics; keep_alive display deferred because it's a private field on OllamaProvider behind Arc<dyn Provider>; 3.2 revealed a real bug — the streaming path discarded final_perf so the panel would always read None until PerfMetrics was threaded through StreamEvent::MessageDelta.

nodes.label: Provider Switch Dialog (Ctrl+W)
nodes.rationale: Scoped to locally-installed Ollama models because App has no Config access and cloud API keys live in Config; a genuine AgentService::set_provider mutator was added because naively rebuilding AgentService would silently drop the tool registry, approval callback, compaction pool, and tool-result cache.

nodes.label: ollama-rs Integration Plan
nodes.rationale: Adds a native Ollama provider additively — Ollama stays usable via the OpenAI-compatible shim — under non-negotiable compatibility constraints: Provider trait unchanged, factory default resolution unchanged, all new fields Option<T> defaulting to None so other providers see zero behavior change.

nodes.label: ollama-rs Crate
nodes.rationale: Built on reqwest 0.12, incompatible with the crate's reqwest 0.11 ProviderError::HttpError — network errors therefore map to ApiError{status:0} and are never retried by retry_with_backoff.

nodes.label: OllamaProvider (Native)
nodes.rationale: The native /api/chat API unlocks what the OpenAI-compat shim never returns: model management (list/pull/show/delete), pull progress, keep_alive, num_ctx, embeddings, typed multimodal input, and native performance metrics (total/load/prompt_eval/eval durations).

nodes.label: PerfMetrics
nodes.rationale: All fields are Option<T> defaulting to None so providers that don't expose runtime metrics (Anthropic, OpenAI, Qwen, Azure) have zero behavior or display change; stored as JSON in a nullable DB column since the metrics are informative, not analytical; tokens/sec derived as eval_count / eval_duration.

nodes.label: Model Download Dialog (Ctrl+D)
nodes.rationale: Ollama exposes no online catalog-search API, so the dialog is repo:tag name entry assisted by installed models plus a hard-coded curated list (CURATED_MODELS), not hub search; cancellation via JoinHandle::abort() on the pull task (no CancellationToken needed); one active pull at a time.

nodes.label: Ollama Embeddings Capability
nodes.rationale: Exposed only as a raw capability (generate_embeddings + crustly ollama embed) because Crustly has no RAG/retrieval layer to attach it to — verified that no embedding reference existed in the code before this phase.

nodes.label: Local LLM & Catwalk Analysis
nodes.rationale: Found that Ollama and LM Studio were absent from the original specification (a new user requirement) while Catwalk integration was a Priority-1 CRITICAL spec requirement; recommended implementing Catwalk first, then local LLM support as optional enhancement.

nodes.label: Proposed Ollama Provider
nodes.rationale: Early (Oct 2025) sketch of an OllamaProvider using raw reqwest against /api/generate and /api/chat, no extra dependencies — predates the later ollama-rs based design.

nodes.label: AgentService
nodes.author: Jeremy JEANNE
nodes.rationale: Central orchestrator for AI conversations: tool execution loop capped at 10 iterations for loop protection; approval check combines requires_approval, auto_approve flags, and user callback.

nodes.label: Provider Trait
nodes.author: Jeremy JEANNE
nodes.rationale: Unified interface (complete/stream/cost/context_window/capability flags) so all LLM backends are interchangeable behind Arc<dyn Provider>.

nodes.label: Tool Trait
nodes.author: Jeremy JEANNE
nodes.rationale: 21 tools implement name/description/input_schema/capabilities/requires_approval/execute; capability enum plus a flat requires_approval boolean drive the approval system.

nodes.label: PromptAnalyzer
nodes.author: Jeremy JEANNE
nodes.rationale: Regex-based keyword detection injects TOOL HINT text into prompts to steer the LLM toward the right tool (plan, read_file, grep, etc.) without an extra model call.

nodes.label: Streaming Architecture
nodes.author: Jeremy JEANNE
nodes.rationale: Tokens flow over an unbounded mpsc channel from drain_stream_to_response to the TUI; forwarder_handle is awaited before ResponseComplete is emitted, guaranteeing all ResponseChunk events are already in the TUI channel — FIFO ordering with no race.

nodes.label: Reasoning/Thinking Display Pipeline
nodes.author: Jeremy JEANNE
nodes.rationale: Three sources unified into ContentBlock::Thinking; priority logic in from_openai_response prefers the reasoning_content field (content preserved verbatim) and only falls back to <think> tag stripping when it's absent; route_text_delta hides in-think text from the live stream, with extract_think_tags as a post-stream safety net.

nodes.label: extract_think_tags
nodes.author: Jeremy JEANNE
nodes.rationale: Case-sensitive by design (<think> only) to match DeepSeek/QwQ output; an unclosed <think> tag treats the rest of the string as thinking.

nodes.label: SubAgentLauncher Trait
nodes.author: Jeremy JEANNE
nodes.rationale: Injected into ToolExecutionContext by AgentService so AgentTool can spawn sub-agents without knowing AgentService internals; launched sub-agents get allow_sub_agents=false to prevent infinite recursion.

nodes.label: Repository Pattern
nodes.author: Jeremy JEANNE
nodes.rationale: Session/Message/Plan/File repositories abstract SQLite access from the service layer — cleaner separation than the Go original per the spec review.

nodes.label: Read-Only Mode
nodes.author: Jeremy JEANNE
nodes.rationale: Plan-mode restriction: write_file/edit_file/execute_code/notebook_edit/agent blocked outright; bash filters unsafe commands; powershell restricted to an allowlist of safe cmdlets.

nodes.label: Catwalk Provider Registry Service
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for AI provider metadata so client apps don't hardcode configs; provider JSON embedded via go:embed for single-binary zero-config deployment; nightly GitHub Actions keep OpenRouter's 200+ models current; Prometheus metrics built in.

nodes.label: Crustly Final Specification v3.0
nodes.rationale: Final spec incorporating all 12 critical enhancements from the specification review to reach 95%+ feature parity with Crush; sets aggressive Rust performance targets (<50ms startup, <25MB idle memory, <15MB binary).

nodes.label: Catwalk Integration (Spec)
nodes.rationale: Priority-1 CRITICAL: CatwalkClient + update_providers_from_catwalk keep provider/model configs current without code changes or manual updates.

nodes.label: Context File Loading
nodes.rationale: Loads .cursorrules, .claudemd, .crustly, CONTEXT.md and injects them ahead of the user prompt — parity with Crush's context file support that was missing from the initial Crustly spec.

nodes.label: Shell Detection System
nodes.rationale: Cross-platform detection (bash/zsh/fish/PowerShell/cmd) with per-shell argument escaping so the bash tool works safely on every OS.

nodes.label: Secret Management (zeroize)
nodes.rationale: ApiKey wrapper is zeroized on drop so API keys are cleared from memory rather than lingering after use.

nodes.label: Profiling Support (pprof)
nodes.rationale: Optional pprof feature flag with flamegraph output — Rust equivalent of Crush's Go pprof support, kept out of the default build to avoid bloating the binary.

nodes.label: Implementation Summary
nodes.rationale: Records that all 12 review-identified enhancements were folded into the final spec (32 new files, +10 sprint days), declaring the specification approved and ready for Sprint 0.

nodes.label: Plan Mode
nodes.rationale: Breaks complex multi-step tasks into structured, reviewable plans so the user has full visibility and control (approve/reject/cancel) before anything executes; tasks run sequentially in validated dependency order with circular-dependency rejection.

nodes.label: PLAN.md Export
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated on approval as living documentation of tasks and implementation steps; overwritten by each new approval, so users must rename plans they want to keep.

nodes.label: Specification Review (Crustly vs Crush)
nodes.rationale: Feature-by-feature gap analysis found 87% parity and 12 critical gaps (tool docs, context files, missing dialogs, Catwalk, shell detection, profiling, etc.); approved the spec conditional on ~23 days of enhancements to reach 95%+ parity.

nodes.label: Tool Approval System
nodes.rationale: Interactive approval gives users full control over dangerous AI tool actions (file writes, shell commands). Dangerous capabilities (WriteFiles, ExecuteShell, SystemModification) always require approval by default; safe tools like read_file skip approval. Checks occur at three levels: tool, agent service, and user.

nodes.label: Approval Callback (async callback pattern)
nodes.rationale: Async callback lets the agent service wait non-blockingly for the user's decision via async/await, staying compatible with streaming responses while decoupling the agent from the TUI.

nodes.label: Channel-Based Communication
nodes.rationale: Each approval request carries its own mpsc response channel, giving a clean async/await flow with no shared mutable state between the agent service and the TUI.

nodes.label: Capability-Based Permissions
nodes.rationale: Tools declare capabilities; dangerous capabilities automatically require approval. Chosen for extensibility so future tool types inherit correct security behavior without per-tool policy code.

nodes.label: Modal Approval Dialog
nodes.rationale: Full-screen modal prevents any other interaction, forcing focus on the security decision; two-view mode (simple vs detailed JSON) balances quick decisions against thorough review.

nodes.label: Auto-Approve Mode
nodes.rationale: Bypass mechanism kept only for trusted/testing scenarios (--auto-approve flag or with_auto_approve_tools); explicitly flagged as dangerous and not recommended for normal use.

nodes.label: Agent Service Integration (approval)
nodes.rationale: Three design options were weighed for getting approval decisions into the agent service: (A) pass event sender into AgentService, (B) callback function, (C) keep it in the TUI layer via ApprovalRequired errors and retry. Option B (approval callback) was recommended and ultimately implemented because the agent service lacks access to the TUI event sender.

nodes.label: Windows MSVC dlltool Build Issue
nodes.rationale: cargo clippy could not run because the Windows MSVC toolchain lacked MinGW tools (dlltool.exe not found); explicitly assessed as an environment setup issue, not a code quality problem.

nodes.label: Multi-Provider Support
nodes.rationale: Rated critical because users expect multi-provider support as advertised — config supports 6+ providers but only Anthropic worked, making it a production blocker for 1.0.

nodes.label: Error Recovery & Resilience
nodes.rationale: Rated critical because the implementation could crash or hang on network issues; production apps need retry with exponential backoff, timeouts, rate-limit handling, and crash recovery.

nodes.label: Security Hardening
nodes.rationale: Rated critical because handling user code and API keys requires robust security — keys were stored in plaintext; plan includes OS keyring storage, path validation, bash sanitization, tool blacklist, and audit log.

nodes.label: Enhanced Tool System
nodes.rationale: Only 3 tools (read, write, bash) existed — too limited for real coding workflows; plan adds List, Search, Git, WebFetch, Editor, Diff, Test, and Lint tools.

nodes.label: Approval System v2 Enhancements
nodes.rationale: v1 approval is functional but limited; v2 adds session memory, whitelists, diff preview, approval history, bulk approve, pattern matching, dry run, and audit export to improve workflow.

nodes.label: Local LLM Integration
nodes.rationale: Local LLM support (LM Studio, Ollama) is a key differentiator but was documented yet untested; verification and auto-detection of localhost providers required before it can be claimed.

nodes.label: MCP Protocol Support
nodes.rationale: MCP enables ecosystem extensions (server/client protocol, stdio/HTTP/WebSocket transports, MCP tool adapter) but is medium priority since it is not critical for core functionality.

nodes.label: LSP Integration
nodes.rationale: LSP adds code intelligence (definitions, references, diagnostics via tower-lsp) but requires significant effort; classified nice-to-have at medium priority.

nodes.label: Plugin System (WASM)
nodes.rationale: WASM-based plugin runtime with sandboxing deferred to lowest priority: a major 7-10 day undertaking that benefits mostly power users and developers.

nodes.label: Quick Wins (High Value, Low Effort)
nodes.rationale: Five ~6-hour fixes prioritized for immediate impact: fix hard-coded model in render.rs, custom config path support, connection timeout, approval timeout, and a first database benchmark.

nodes.label: Plan Mode
nodes.rationale: Inspired by Claude Code's planning capabilities: the LLM explores the codebase read-only, produces a structured plan with subtasks, and executes only after explicit user approval. Goals: safer execution, better task management, user architectural control, progress tracking, and flexibility to use different models for planning vs execution.

nodes.label: Plan Mode Tool Restrictions
nodes.rationale: In Plan mode only read-only tools are allowed (read_file, ls, glob, grep, safe bash commands); write tools and mutating bash (redirects, pipes, git commit) are blocked by checking tool capabilities against the app mode in ToolExecutionContext, preventing uncontrolled modifications during exploration.

nodes.label: Priority Matrix
nodes.rationale: Quick-reference effort-vs-impact quadrant view of the roadmap: overall grade C+ (functional prototype, not production-ready); show-stoppers for 1.0 were single-provider support, crashes on network errors, plaintext API keys, untested local LLM, and a hard-coded model bug.

nodes.label: Project Rename: crusty to crustly
nodes.rationale: Full rebrand across folder, Cargo.toml, source (CrustyError to CrustlyError), env vars (CRUSTY_* to CRUSTLY_*), config paths, docs, and logo; one 'crusty' reference intentionally kept in README as a croissant pun.

nodes.label: Startup Splash Screen
nodes.rationale: Adds professional branding at launch (Rust crab ASCII art, version, model, provider); dismissed by any keypress with no timeout to respect the user's reading pace. Implemented as src/tui/splash.rs with a Splash variant added to AppMode.

nodes.label: Sprint 0: Project Setup and Initialization
nodes.rationale: Stub-first scaffolding approach: 30+ files across 17 module directories created before implementation, which the team noted worked well; SQLite conflict resolved by dropping rusqlite in favor of sqlx only.

nodes.label: Crabrace Integration (provider registry)
nodes.rationale: Provider registry successfully migrated from Catwalk to Crabrace; exposes fetch_providers(), health_check(), get_provider() via a local path dependency.

nodes.label: Error Handling System (CrustlyError + ErrorCode)
nodes.rationale: Custom error enum with 12 numeric error codes (ConfigNotFound=1000, ProviderAuthFailed=2001, etc.) using thiserror, for categorized, user-friendly errors from the start.

nodes.label: OpenAI Provider
nodes.rationale: 517-line implementation of the Provider trait supporting the official OpenAI API, custom endpoints, and local LLMs (LM Studio, Ollama) via OpenAIProvider::local(); includes SSE streaming, tool use, and per-model cost calculation.

nodes.label: Approval Timeout (auto-deny)
nodes.rationale: Approval requests auto-deny after 5 minutes so stale requests cannot leave the app in limbo; adds a color-coded visual countdown (green >3min, yellow 1-3min, red <1min) in the dialog.

nodes.label: Database Benchmark Suite (criterion)
nodes.rationale: First performance baselines: parameterized session/message create-get-list benchmarks (10-500 records) using criterion, enabling measurement before optimization.

nodes.label: Retry Logic with Exponential Backoff
nodes.rationale: src/llm/provider/retry.rs (426 lines): exponential backoff with jitter, selective retry distinguishing transient errors (network, 429, timeout, 5xx) from permanent ones (401, 400, 404) that fail fast; stream retry applies only to the initial connection since mid-stream retry is impossible.

nodes.label: Rate Limit Detection & Handling
nodes.rationale: Extracts Retry-After headers (which may be seconds or a date) from 429 responses, converts to ProviderError::RateLimitExceeded, and respects server-specified wait times with a fallback default.

nodes.label: Database Lock Recovery
nodes.rationale: src/db/retry.rs (365 lines): detects SQLite BUSY/LOCKED errors and retries with exponential backoff (5 attempts, 50ms-5s), plus busy_timeout=5000 on the connection string and 10s pool acquire_timeout for concurrent access.

nodes.label: Error Reporting Infrastructure (ErrorInfo)
nodes.rationale: Structured ErrorInfo with severity levels (Info/Warning/Error/Critical) and categories (Network, Database, Config, Input, Tool, Internal), color-coded display, and retry tracking (is_retryable, retry_count, next_retry) in src/tui/error.rs.

nodes.label: Database Layer (SQLite + SQLx)
nodes.rationale: Design decisions: Unix timestamps over ISO strings for simplicity and performance; foreign key cascades for automatic cleanup; archive (soft delete) instead of hard delete for sessions; connection pool capped at 5 for SQLite WAL mode; in-memory database support for fast tests.

nodes.label: Repository Pattern
nodes.rationale: Session, Message, and File repositories behind a common async Repository<T> trait provide clean separation between data access and business logic; prepared statements via SQLx give type-safe, injection-resistant queries.

nodes.label: Token & Cost Tracking
nodes.rationale: Message schema tracks input/output/reasoning/cache_creation/cache_read tokens and cost as optional fields to stay flexible across model types, including prompt caching support.

nodes.label: Service Layer (Session/Message/File services)
nodes.rationale: ServiceContext for shared resources plus ServiceManager for centralized access, with clean separation between services and repositories; includes automatic message sequence numbering and per-message usage statistics.

nodes.label: Model Type Alignment
nodes.rationale: Service and database layers disagreed on types (String vs Uuid ids, i64 vs DateTime<Utc>). Chose to modernize the database models rather than downgrade the services: custom FromRow implementations convert SQLite TEXT/INTEGER storage to Uuid/DateTime/PathBuf, with a migration to transform existing data.

nodes.label: Provider Abstraction Layer
nodes.rationale: A Provider trait (complete, stream, supports_streaming, supports_tools) with common LLMRequest/LLMResponse/ContentBlock types isolates the app from vendor APIs so Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and Bedrock backends are interchangeable.

nodes.label: Agent Service
nodes.rationale: Orchestration layer between the UI and providers: manages conversation context, tool execution approval, response streaming, token usage tracking, and persisting messages to the database.

nodes.label: Tool Framework (Tool trait + ToolRegistry)
nodes.rationale: Async Tool trait (name, description, parameters, execute, requires_approval) with a HashMap-backed ToolRegistry; requires_approval on the trait is the hook the approval system builds on.

nodes.label: Terminal User Interface (Ratatui)
nodes.rationale: Ratatui-based ChatGPT/Claude-like terminal experience: four-panel layout (header, chat, input, status bar), mode-based navigation (Chat/SessionList/Help/Settings), and mpsc event channels so agent responses never block the UI.

nodes.label: Event-Driven TUI Architecture
nodes.rationale: All interactions flow through a TuiEvent enum and unbounded async channels; user messages spawn background tokio tasks so agent processing never blocks rendering, and rendering only happens on state changes or events.

nodes.label: Component Wiring (CLI to TUI)
nodes.rationale: Dependency-injection style assembly: CLI parses args, config loads with priority (defaults, system config, local config, env vars), database migrates on startup, AnthropicProvider + ToolRegistry (Read/Write/Bash) are injected into AgentService via builder pattern, then the TUI launches.

nodes.label: Sprint 8: Enhanced Testing
nodes.rationale: Grew tests from 139 to 182 (+31%) with CLI (24), streaming (10), and error scenario (9) suites; TUI component tests deferred because mocking a terminal backend is complex and manual testing already covers it.

nodes.label: Mock Providers (Streaming/Error/Working)
nodes.rationale: StreamingMockProvider, ErrorMockProvider, and WorkingMockProvider implement the Provider trait so tests need no API calls: fast (<3s total), deterministic, and able to simulate rate limits, timeouts, and malformed responses.

nodes.label: Markdown Rendering (pulldown-cmark)
nodes.rationale: src/tui/markdown.rs parses markdown to Ratatui widgets: headings, bordered code blocks with language labels, inline code highlighting, and horizontal rules integrated into chat message rendering.

nodes.label: Syntax Highlighting (syntect)
nodes.rationale: src/tui/highlight.rs uses syntect with lazy-loaded syntax sets (loaded once at startup to avoid per-render cost), supports 100+ languages with the Base16 Ocean Dark theme, line numbers, and graceful fallback for unknown languages.

nodes.label: Testing Summary
nodes.rationale: Canonical test inventory: 182 automated tests (130 unit + 9 integration + 24 CLI + 10 streaming + 9 error) plus a 9-scenario manual testing guide for real API validation; in-memory SQLite chosen for test speed and isolation.

nodes.label: Windows dlltool.exe Build Issue
nodes.rationale: Known Rust MSVC toolchain issue on Windows when crates need MinGW tools; workarounds are MinGW-w64 install, WSL2, Linux/macOS, or the GNU toolchain.

nodes.label: Crabrace Provider Registry Server
nodes.rationale: Crabrace (Rust port of Catwalk) replaces the originally planned Catwalk integration because it offers 2.5x higher throughput, 2x faster responses, Rust memory safety, and local LLM support. Automatic provider discovery avoids outdated manual provider config, missing cost metadata, and manual maintenance.

nodes.label: Automatic Provider Discovery
nodes.rationale: Dynamic fetching of providers and model metadata (capabilities, pricing, limits) so models never go stale, new providers need no code changes, and configuration is zero-maintenance (18 providers, 354+ models).

nodes.label: Conditional File Logging
nodes.rationale: Log files are only created when debug mode (-d) is explicitly enabled, to keep the workspace clean, avoid privacy issues (logs contain user data), avoid disk bloat (7-day auto-cleanup), and stay silent so logging never interferes with the TUI. Logs live in a git-ignored local .crustly/logs/ folder.

nodes.label: Rust tracing Ecosystem
nodes.rationale: Chosen for high-performance structured logging with minimal overhead when disabled (tracing, tracing-subscriber, tracing-appender).

nodes.label: LM Studio Local LLM Server
nodes.rationale: Local LLMs are supported for 100% privacy (code never leaves the machine), zero cost, offline use, and no rate limits, at the price of slower responses and 16GB+ RAM requirements versus cloud models.

nodes.label: OPENAI_BASE_URL Environment Variable
nodes.rationale: Single environment variable redirects the OpenAI provider to any OpenAI-compatible local server (LM Studio, Ollama, LocalAI, Text Generation WebUI) with no extra setup; the /v1 suffix is required.

nodes.label: Prompt Analyzer
nodes.rationale: Automatically detects keywords in user prompts and appends explicit tool hints before sending to the LLM, to ensure correct tool usage and reduce ambiguity. Transparent (user sees the original prompt, LLM gets the enhanced one) and non-intrusive (only activates on keyword detection). Implemented in src/tui/prompt_analyzer.rs, integrated via src/tui/app.rs send_message.

nodes.label: Regex Keyword Detection
nodes.rationale: Regex-based keyword matching with word boundaries and case-insensitive detection maps prompt phrases to tool hints (plan, read_file, grep, write_file, edit_file, bash, web_search); supports multiple tool detection per prompt.

nodes.label: QwenProvider
nodes.rationale: Native Qwen LLM integration supporting both local deployment (vLLM, LM Studio, Ollama) and DashScope cloud API, using OpenAI-compatible request format for broad server compatibility.

nodes.label: Hermes-Style Tool Calling
nodes.rationale: XML <tool_call> tag parsing recommended for Qwen3 via vLLM because it is optimized for those models, gives better structured reasoning, and higher tool call accuracy than OpenAI-style parsing.

nodes.label: Native Qwen-Agent Tool Format
nodes.rationale: Official Qwen-Agent Unicode-marker format; chosen when direct compatibility with Qwen internal function calling, native parallel function calls, and stop-word handling are needed.

nodes.label: JSON-to-Database Plan Storage Migration
nodes.rationale: Planned follow-up: complete the database repository and migrate plan persistence from JSON to the DB for better scalability and reliability; alternative quick win is supporting multiple concurrent plans by changing the filename pattern.

nodes.label: Plan Mode Sequential Task Execution
nodes.rationale: Workflow: AI builds a structured plan (plan tool, add_task, finalize), the user reviews and approves (Ctrl+A) or rejects (Ctrl+R), then tasks auto-execute sequentially in dependency order with state Pending -> InProgress -> Completed, persisted after each task so interrupted executions can be resumed.

nodes.label: Topological Sort of Task Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Tasks execute in dependency order via topological sort so no task starts before its dependencies complete.

nodes.label: Circular Dependency Detection
nodes.rationale: Validation blocks finalizing plans containing dependency cycles, preventing execution deadlock; a clear 'Circular dependency detected' error is surfaced.

nodes.label: .crustly_plan.json State File
nodes.rationale: Plan state (task statuses, timestamps, approval/rejection) is persisted to .crustly_plan.json after every task update so interrupted executions survive force-quit and can be resumed or restarted.

nodes.label: Plan Mode Read-Only Tool Restriction
nodes.rationale: While planning, write operations are blocked ('Write operations not allowed in Plan mode') and only read-only tools (ls, read_file, grep) work, so plans cannot mutate the workspace before approval.
